To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effect of MNCs’ breadth on multinationality is contingent on host market uncertainty, subsidiary asset specificity and the level of FDI.
multinationality generates value in the presence of host market uncertainty, and that the effect of multinationality value on FDI breadth depends on the degree of subsidiary asset specificity.

the value of FDI breadth for a MNC is negatively associated with the depth of its subsidiaries and their sales in the host country and positively associated with the extent to which its subsidiaries engage in intra-firm trade.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the value of multinational operations is contingent on FDI structure, subsidiary asset specificity, and host market uncertainty.
how MNCs manage and coordinate their global operations to maximize value creation.
the value of multinational firms and the conditions that determine the value of multinational operations for firms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the value of multinationaly is contingent on the degree to which the MNC is committed to its host country and the extent to which the subsidiary has developed intra-firm linkages with other subsidiaries in other countries.
multinationality is valuable under host market uncertainty when subsidiaries are not too committed and when they have strong links with other subsidiaries.
the effect of multinationality on MNCs’ performance is conditional and contingent upon a number of factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the value of multinational operations is conditional upon the level of country- and subsidiary-level asset specificity, which is consistent with the notion of MNCs as a bundle of resources and capabilities.
the value of multinational diversification is contingent upon the level of host country uncertainty and the degree of subsidiary asset specificity.
the value of multinationaly is not a given, but rather a contingent outcome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FDI breadth is more valuable in the presence of intra-firm trade and local commitment, which are important but less explored factors in the literature.
the value of multinational operations is contingent on FDI depth, local sales, and trade links to other MNC subsidiaries.

MNCs’ investment specificity in terms of FPI and local sales, and the extent to which they are integrated into their parent firms’ intra-firm networks are important factors in determining the value of multinational operations.
